title: Fix Trinity Plugin Port Key Delimiter Mismatch
description: trinity/plugin/rs/lib.rs has two duplicated local helper pairs (port_endpoint/split_endpoint, ~line 296 in app_jack and ~line 2085 in app_rewrite) that hardcode ':' as the node/port delimiter when building/parsing Edge.source/Edge.target strings. trinity_ram's own port_key/parse_port_key convention was changed from 'nodeId:portId' to 'nodeId@portId' during the Unified Token-Efficient DSL Syntax ticket (Wave 2), but trinity/plugin was out of that ticket's file scope, so these local helpers were left behind and now silently misparse real port-key strings coming out of trinity_ram (e.g. in fixture_to_media_graph). This was flagged as a deferred follow-up in that ticket's closing summary (task_11e64f5b). Fix: delete both duplicated local helper pairs and delegate to trinity_ram::port_key/trinity_ram::parse_port_key (or port_node_id/port_port_id) directly. Also fix two hardcoded 'nodeId:portId'-style test fixture literals in app_rewrite's lhs_semantic_graph_fixture (~line 1930: "lhs-match:out", "lhs-where:in") which are Edge.source/target values, not display labels. Run `cargo test -p trinity-plugin` after.
summary: Deleted the two duplicated port_endpoint/split_endpoint helper pairs in trinity/plugin/rs/lib.rs (app_jack ~line 296, app_rewrite ~line 2080) that hardcoded ':' as the node/port delimiter. Both now delegate to trinity_ram::port_key/trinity_ram::parse_port_key, matching the '@' convention trinity_ram switched to during the Unified Token-Efficient DSL Syntax ticket (mirrors the same delegation pattern already used in trinity/rewrite/engine/rs/lib.rs). Also fixed two hardcoded "nodeId:portId"-style Edge.source/target test-fixture literals in app_rewrite's lhs_semantic_graph_fixture ("lhs-match:out"/"lhs-where:in" -> "lhs-match@out"/"lhs-where@in"). Ran `cargo test -p trinity-plugin`: all 36 unit tests pass. A separate doctest run failed on a stale libvcs.rlib extern-location error, unrelated to this change (no doctests exist in the touched code; likely concurrent workspace rebuild elsewhere).
